audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 4, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for administrative hierarchy, regional provisioning, royal marriages, tribute, imperial reach, court consumption, animal systems, militarization, public security, wisdom claims, and knowledge of creation.

verses.restored: King Solomon was king over all Israel.

familiar.text: So king Solomon was king over all Israel.

modern.text: So King Solomon ruled over Israel,

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מֶ֖לֶךְ עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: These were officials he had: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest;

familiar.text: And these were the princes which he had; Azariah the son of Zadok the priest,

modern.text: and these were his chief officials: Azariah son of Zadok was the priest;

original.text: וְאֵ֥לֶּה הַשָּׂרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁר ל֑וֹ עֲזַרְיָ֥הוּ בֶן צָד֖וֹק הַכֹּהֵֽן

verses.restored: Elihoreph and Ahijah sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, recorder.

familiar.text: Elihoreph and Ahiah, the sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud, the recorder.

modern.text: Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, were secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;

original.text: אֱלִיחֹ֧רֶף וַאֲחִיָּ֛ה בְּנֵ֥י שִׁישָׁ֖א סֹפְרִ֑ים יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בֶּן אֲחִיל֖וּד הַמַּזְכִּֽיר

verses.restored: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over army; Zadok and Abiathar were priests.

familiar.text: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the host: and Zadok and Abiathar were the priests:

modern.text: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the army; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;

original.text: וּבְנָיָ֥הוּ בֶן יְהוֹיָדָ֖ע עַל הַצָּבָ֑א וְצָד֥וֹק וְאֶבְיָתָ֖ר כֹּהֲנִֽים

verses.restored: Azariah son of Nathan was over administrators; Zabud son of Nathan was priest/chief official and king's friend.

familiar.text: And Azariah the son of Nathan was over the officers: and Zabud the son of Nathan was principal officer, and the king’s friend:

modern.text: Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the governors; Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and adviser to the king;

original.text: וַעֲזַרְיָ֥הוּ בֶן נָתָ֖ן עַל הַנִּצָּבִ֑ים וְזָב֧וּד בֶּן נָתָ֛ן כֹּהֵ֖ן רֵעֶ֥ה הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Ahishar was over household; Adoniram son of Abda was over forced labor/tribute.

familiar.text: And Ahishar was over the household: and Adoniram the son of Abda was over the tribute.

modern.text: Ahishar was in charge of the palace; and Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of the forced labor. Solomon’s Twelve Officers

original.text: וַאֲחִישָׁ֖ר עַל הַבָּ֑יִת וַאֲדֹנִירָ֥ם בֶּן עַבְדָּ֖א עַל הַמַּֽס

verses.restored: Solomon had twelve administrators over all Israel. They provided food for king and his household; each provided for one month in year.

familiar.text: And Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, which provided victuals for the king and his household: each man his month in a year made provision.

modern.text: Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel to provide food for the king and his household. Each one would arrange provisions for one month of the year,

original.text: וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֞ה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂ֤ר נִצָּבִים֙ עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְכִלְכְּל֥וּ אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְאֶת בֵּית֑וֹ חֹ֧דֶשׁ בַּשָּׁנָ֛ה יִהְיֶ֥ה עַל אחד לְכַלְכֵּֽל

verses.restored: These are their names: Ben-hur in hill country of Ephraim;

familiar.text: And these are their names: The son of Hur, in mount Ephraim:

modern.text: and these were their names: Ben-hur in the hill country of Ephraim;

original.text: וְאֵ֣לֶּה שְׁמוֹתָ֔ם בֶּן ח֖וּר בְּהַ֥ר אֶפְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: Ben-deker in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan;

familiar.text: The son of Dekar, in Makaz, and in Shaalbim, and Bethshemesh, and Elonbethhanan:

modern.text: Ben-deker in Makaz, in Shaalbim, in Beth-shemesh, and in Elon-beth-hanan;

original.text: בֶּן דֶּ֛קֶר בְּמָקַ֥ץ וּבְשַֽׁעַלְבִ֖ים וּבֵ֣ית שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וְאֵיל֖וֹן בֵּ֥ית חָנָֽן

verses.restored: Ben-hesed in Arubboth; Socoh and all land of Hepher were his.

familiar.text: The son of Hesed, in Aruboth; to him pertained Sochoh, and all the land of Hepher:

modern.text: Ben-hesed in Arubboth (Socoh and all the land of Hepher belonged to him);

original.text: בֶּן חֶ֖סֶד בָּֽאֲרֻבּ֑וֹת ל֥וֹ שֹׂכֹ֖ה וְכָל אֶ֥רֶץ חֵֽפֶר

verses.restored: Ben-abinadab in all heights/region of Dor; Taphath daughter of Solomon was his wife.

familiar.text: The son of Abinadab, in all the region of Dor; which had Taphath the daughter of Solomon to wife:

modern.text: Ben-abinadab in Naphath-dor (Taphath, a daughter of Solomon, was his wife);

original.text: בֶּן אֲבִֽינָדָ֖ב כָּל נָ֣פַת דֹּ֑אר טָפַת֙ בַּת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה הָ֥יְתָה לּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: Baana son of Ahilud had Taanach, Megiddo, and all Beth-shean beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and beyond Jokmeam.

familiar.text: Baana the son of Ahilud; to him pertained Taanach and Megiddo, and all Bethshean, which is by Zartanah beneath Jezreel, from Bethshean to Abelmeholah, even unto the place that is beyond Jokneam:

modern.text: Baana son of Ahilud in Taanach, in Megiddo, and in all of Beth-shean next to Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and on past Jokmeam;

original.text: בַּֽעֲנָא֙ בֶּן אֲחִיל֔וּד תַּעְנַ֖ךְ וּמְגִדּ֑וֹ וְכָל בֵּ֣ית שְׁאָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ אֵ֨צֶל צָרְתַ֜נָה מִתַּ֣חַת לְיִזְרְעֶ֗אל מִבֵּ֤ית שְׁאָן֙ עַ֚ד אָבֵ֣ל מְחוֹלָ֔ה עַ֖ד מֵעֵ֥בֶר לְיָקְמֳעָֽם

verses.restored: Ben-geber was in Ramoth-gilead; towns of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead were his, and region of Argob in Bashan—sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars.

familiar.text: The son of Geber, in Ramothgilead; to him pertained the towns of Jair the son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead; to him also pertained the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, threescore great cities with walls and brasen bars:

modern.text: Ben-geber in Ramoth-gilead (the villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead belonged to him, as well as the region of Argob in Bashan with its sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars);

original.text: בֶּן גֶּ֖בֶר בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד ל֡וֹ חַוֺּת֩ יָאִ֨יר בֶּן מְנַשֶּׁ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּגִּלְעָ֗ד ל֚וֹ חֶ֤בֶל אַרְגֹּב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּבָּשָׁ֔ן שִׁשִּׁים֙ עָרִ֣ים גְּדֹל֔וֹת חוֹמָ֖ה וּבְרִ֥יחַ נְחֹֽשֶׁת

verses.restored: Ahinadab son of Iddo was in Mahanaim.

familiar.text: Ahinadab the son of Iddo had Mahanaim:

modern.text: Ahinadab son of Iddo in Mahanaim;

original.text: אֲחִֽינָדָ֥ב בֶּן עִדֹּ֖א מַחֲנָֽיְמָה

verses.restored: Ahimaaz was in Naphtali; he also took Basemath daughter of Solomon as wife.

familiar.text: Ahimaaz was in Naphtali; he also took Basmath the daughter of Solomon to wife:

modern.text: Ahimaaz in Naphtali (he had married Basemath, a daughter of Solomon);

original.text: אֲחִימַ֖עַץ בְּנַפְתָּלִ֑י גַּם ה֗וּא לָקַ֛ח אֶת בָּשְׂמַ֥ת בַּת שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: Baana son of Hushai was in Asher and Bealoth.

familiar.text: Baanah the son of Hushai was in Asher and in Aloth:

modern.text: Baana son of Hushai in Asher and in Aloth;

original.text: בַּֽעֲנָא֙ בֶּן חוּשָׁ֔י בְּאָשֵׁ֖ר וּבְעָלֽוֹת

verses.restored: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was in Issachar.

familiar.text: Jehoshaphat the son of Paruah, in Issachar:

modern.text: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah in Issachar;

original.text: יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בֶּן פָּר֖וּחַ בְּיִשָׂשכָֽר

verses.restored: Shimei son of Ela was in Benjamin.

familiar.text: Shimei the son of Elah, in Benjamin:

modern.text: Shimei son of Ela in Benjamin;

original.text: שִׁמְעִ֥י בֶן אֵלָ֖א בְּבִנְיָמִֽן

verses.restored: Geber son of Uri was in land of Gilead, land of Sihon king of Amorites and Og king of Bashan; one administrator was over land.

familiar.text: Geber the son of Uri was in the country of Gilead, in the country of Sihon king of the Amorites, and of Og king of Bashan; and he was the only officer which was in the land.

modern.text: Geber son of Uri in the land of Gilead, including the territories of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan. There was also one governor in the land of Judah. Solomon’s Prosperity

original.text: גֶּ֥בֶר בֶּן אֻרִ֖י בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גִּלְעָ֑ד אֶ֜רֶץ סִיח֣וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֗י וְעֹג֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֔ן וּנְצִ֥יב אֶחָ֖ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: Judah and Israel were many, like sand beside sea in multitude, eating, drinking, and rejoicing.

familiar.text: Judah and Israel were many, as the sand which is by the sea in multitude, eating and drinking, and making merry.

modern.text: The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore, and they were eating and drinking and rejoicing.

original.text: יְהוּדָ֤ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ רַבִּ֔ים כַּח֥וֹל אֲשֶׁר עַל הַיָּ֖ם לָרֹ֑ב אֹכְלִ֥ים וְשֹׁתִ֖ים וּשְׂמֵחִֽים

verses.restored: Solomon ruled over all kingdoms from River to land of Philistines and border of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon all days of his life.

familiar.text: And Solomon reigned over all kingdoms from the river unto the land of the Philistines, and unto the border of Egypt: they brought presents, and served Solomon all the days of his life.

modern.text: And Solomon reigned over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt. These kingdoms offered tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.

original.text: וּשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה הָיָ֤ה מוֹשֵׁל֙ בְּכָל הַמַּמְלָכ֔וֹת מִן הַנָּהָר֙ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְעַ֖ד גְּב֣וּל מִצְרָ֑יִם מַגִּשִׁ֥ים מִנְחָ֛ה וְעֹבְדִ֥ים אֶת שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה כָּל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו

verses.restored: Solomon's provision for one day was thirty kors of fine flour and sixty kors of meal,

familiar.text: And Solomon’s provision for one day was thirty measures of fine flour, and threescore measures of meal,

modern.text: Solomon’s provisions for a single day were thirty cors of fine flour, sixty cors of meal,

original.text: וַיְהִ֥י לֶֽחֶם שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְי֣וֹם אֶחָ֑ד שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים כֹּר֙ סֹ֔לֶת וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים כֹּ֖ר קָֽמַח

verses.restored: ten fattened cattle, twenty pasture-fed cattle, one hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened birds.

familiar.text: Ten fat oxen, and twenty oxen out of the pastures, and an hundred sheep, beside harts, and roebucks, and fallowdeer, and fatted fowl.

modern.text: ten fat oxen, twenty range oxen, and a hundred sheep, as well as deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened poultry.

original.text: עֲשָׂרָ֨ה בָקָ֜ר בְּרִאִ֗ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים בָּקָ֛ר רְעִ֖י וּמֵ֣אָה צֹ֑אן לְ֠בַד מֵֽאַיָּ֤ל וּצְבִי֙ וְיַחְמ֔וּר וּבַרְבֻּרִ֖ים אֲבוּסִֽים

verses.restored: He had dominion over all beyond River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all kings beyond River, and had peace from every side around him.

familiar.text: For he had dominion over all the region on this side the river, from Tiphsah even to Azzah, over all the kings on this side the river: and he had peace on all sides round about him.

modern.text: For Solomon had dominion over everything west of the Euphrates —over all the kingdoms from Tiphsah to Gaza—and he had peace on all sides.

original.text: כִּי ה֞וּא רֹדֶ֣ה בְּכָל עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֗ר מִתִּפְסַח֙ וְעַד עַזָּ֔ה בְּכָל מַלְכֵ֖י עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֑ר וְשָׁל֗וֹם הָ֥יָה ל֛וֹ מִכָּל עֲבָרָ֖יו מִסָּבִֽיב

verses.restored: Judah and Israel lived in security, each under vine and fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba, all days of Solomon.

familiar.text: And Judah and Israel dwelt safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.

modern.text: Throughout the days of Solomon, Judah and Israel dwelt securely from Dan to Beersheba, each man under his own vine and his own fig tree.

original.text: וַיֵּשֶׁב֩ יְהוּדָ֨ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לָבֶ֗טַח אִ֣ישׁ תַּ֤חַת גַּפְנוֹ֙ וְתַ֣חַת תְּאֵֽנָת֔וֹ מִדָּ֖ן וְעַד בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹֽה

verses.restored: Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen.

familiar.text: And Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.

modern.text: Solomon had 4,000 stalls for his chariot horses and 12,000 horses.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י לִשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אֻרְוֺ֥ת סוּסִ֖ים לְמֶרְכָּב֑וֹ וּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִֽׁים

verses.restored: Those administrators provided food for King Solomon and all who came to king's table, each in his month; they let nothing be lacking.

familiar.text: And those officers provided victual for king Solomon, and for all that came unto king Solomon’s table, every man in his month: they lacked nothing.

modern.text: Each month the governors in turn provided food for King Solomon and all who came to his table. They saw to it that nothing was lacking.

original.text: וְכִלְכְּלוּ֩ הַנִּצָּבִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה אֶת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה וְאֵ֧ת כָּל הַקָּרֵ֛ב אֶל שֻׁלְחַ֥ן הַמֶּֽלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ חָדְשׁ֑וֹ לֹ֥א יְעַדְּר֖וּ דָּבָֽר

verses.restored: They brought barley and straw for horses and swift steeds to required place, each according to his charge.

familiar.text: Barley also and straw for the horses and dromedaries brought they unto the place where the officers were, every man according to his charge.

modern.text: Each one also brought to the required place their quotas of barley and straw for the chariot horses and other horses. Solomon’s Wisdom

original.text: וְהַשְּׂעֹרִ֣ים וְהַתֶּ֔בֶן לַסּוּסִ֖ים וְלָרָ֑כֶשׁ יָבִ֗אוּ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִֽהְיֶה שָּׁ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ כְּמִשְׁפָּטֽוֹ

verses.restored: Divine gave Solomon very great wisdom and understanding, and breadth of heart like sand upon seashore.

familiar.text: And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore.

modern.text: And God gave Solomon wisdom, exceedingly deep insight, and understanding beyond measure, like the sand on the seashore.

original.text: וַיִּתֵּן֩ אֱלֹהִ֨ים חָכְמָ֧ה לִשְׁלֹמֹ֛ה וּתְבוּנָ֖ה הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וְרֹ֣חַב לֵ֔ב כַּח֕וֹל אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיָּֽם

verses.restored: Solomon's wisdom was greater than wisdom of all children of east and all wisdom of Egypt.

familiar.text: And Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt.

modern.text: Solomon’s wisdom was greater than that of all the men of the East, greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.

original.text: וַתֵּ֨רֶב֙ חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מֵֽחָכְמַ֖ת כָּל בְּנֵי קֶ֑דֶם וּמִכֹּ֖ל חָכְמַ֥ת מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: He was wiser than every human—than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, sons of Mahol—and his name/fame was among all nations around.

familiar.text: For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.

modern.text: He was wiser than all men—wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and wiser than Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. And his fame spread throughout the surrounding nations.

original.text: וַיֶּחְכַּם֮ מִכָּל הָֽאָדָם֒ מֵאֵיתָ֣ן הָאֶזְרָחִ֗י וְהֵימָ֧ן וְכַלְכֹּ֛ל וְדַרְדַּ֖ע בְּנֵ֣י מָח֑וֹל וַיְהִֽי שְׁמ֥וֹ בְכָֽל הַגּוֹיִ֖ם סָבִֽיב

verses.restored: He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were one thousand and five.

familiar.text: And he spake three thousand proverbs: and his songs were a thousand and five.

modern.text: Solomon composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֕ר שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים מָשָׁ֑ל וַיְהִ֥י שִׁיר֖וֹ חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה וָאָֽלֶף

verses.restored: He spoke concerning trees, from cedar in Lebanon to hyssop growing from wall. He spoke concerning animals, birds, creeping things, and fish.

familiar.text: And he spake of trees, from the cedar tree that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall: he spake also of beasts, and of fowl, and of creeping things, and of fishes.

modern.text: He spoke of trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing in the wall, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּר֮ עַל הָֽעֵצִים֒ מִן הָאֶ֨רֶז֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלְּבָנ֔וֹן וְעַד֙ הָאֵז֔וֹב אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֹצֵ֖א בַּקִּ֑יר וַיְדַבֵּר֙ עַל הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה וְעַל הָע֔וֹף וְעַל הָרֶ֖מֶשׂ וְעַל הַדָּגִֽים

verses.restored: People came from all peoples to hear wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of earth who heard his wisdom.

familiar.text: And there came of all people to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth, which had heard of his wisdom.

modern.text: So men of all nations came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ מִכָּל הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים לִשְׁמֹ֕עַ אֵ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה מֵאֵת֙ כָּל מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמְע֖וּ אֶת חָכְמָתֽוֹ

translation_notes: The administrative list is not neutral bureaucracy. It maps who collects food, labor, and resources for the palace and who supervises the people doing that work.
Adoniram's portfolio over forced labor/tribute anticipates the grievance that fractures the kingdom. Administrative efficiency can institutionalize exploitation.
Taphath and Basemath, Solomon's daughters, appear through marriages to regional officials. Their consent and political roles are not recorded.
The image of each person under vine and fig tree preserves a genuine ideal of ordinary security, but it exists beside tribute, imperial service, enormous palace consumption, and military buildup.
Daily court provisions and animal numbers reflect concentrated wealth and extraction. Abundance at the royal table does not prove abundance in every household.
The empire's peoples bring gifts/tribute and serve Solomon. 'Peace' may describe absence of revolt from the center while conquered communities experience domination.
Wisdom includes poetry and close observation of plants and animals. Knowledge of creation must not be confused with ownership or permission to exploit it.
Comparisons that make Solomon wiser than whole regions risk civilizational superiority. Egypt and eastern peoples possess their own wisdom traditions and human dignity.
safety_note: Do not romanticize the administrative machine, tribute, forced labor, militarization, or extravagant court consumption as proof of Divine prosperity. Test royal wisdom by whether ordinary people, workers, neighboring peoples, and animals flourish.
